title: 《身体从未忘记》— 好书精读
title_en: The Body Keeps the Score — Deep Reading

questions.question: 《身体从未忘记》区分了「自上而下」和「自下而上」两条路径。它对创伤治疗的核心建议是什么？
options: 先用认知重评说服自己现在已经安全，然后再配合做一些身体练习
谈话和认知疗法对创伤基本无效，应当全部改用瑜伽、击鼓等身体疗法来取代
先把创伤经历完整地复述出来，身体的警觉反应自然就会慢慢消退
两条路都要走，但常常得先用呼吸、动作、节律让身体安定，再处理叙事
questions.explanation: 创伤状态下，「瞭望塔」前额叶在警报响起时离线，光从认知那边下命令够不着，所以顺序常要倒过来：先身体，后语言。书的论点不是「谈话无用」；文章还提醒，创伤聚焦认知行为疗法至今是证据最充分的一线方案，合理读法是「不止于谈话」。
questions.question_en: The Body Keeps the Score distinguishes top-down from bottom-up routes. What is its core advice for treating trauma?
options_en: First use cognitive reappraisal to convince yourself you're safe now, then add some body exercises
Talk and cognitive therapies basically fail and should be replaced entirely by yoga, drumming, and other body work
First recount the traumatic experience in full, and the body's alarm reactions will fade on their own
Use both, but often settle the body first through breathing, movement, and rhythm before working on the narrative
questions.explanation_en: In trauma the prefrontal 'watchtower' goes offline when the alarm sounds, so commands from the cognitive side can't reach it; the order often has to flip to body first, words second. The book doesn't claim talk is useless, and the article adds that trauma-focused CBT remains the best-evidenced first-line treatment: the right reading is 'not only talk'.

questions.question: 文章认为「身体从未忘记」（身体记分）这个说法最该怎么理解？
options: 身体会逐字记住事件的每个细节，记得比大脑的叙事记忆更准确
神经和内分泌系统的默认设置被调到「战时」那一档并留在那里
创伤记忆被整块压抑在潜意识深处，需要专门的疗法把它挖出来
肌肉和身体组织里储存着事件的记忆，可以通过按摩等方式把它释放出来
questions.explanation: 书名不是说细胞里存着一段录像，而是静息心率、呼吸、肌张力、应激激素基线等被调到战时档且不回落。文章把「肌肉里存着记忆」列为被滥用得最厉害的误读；「挖出被压抑的记忆」也被点名为记忆科学里争议极大的假设——创伤通常是被记得太清楚。
questions.question_en: According to the article, how should the idea that 'the body keeps the score' best be understood?
options_en: The body records every detail of an event verbatim, more accurately than the brain's narrative memory
The nervous and endocrine systems' default settings are switched to a wartime mode and stay there
Traumatic memories are repressed whole in the unconscious and must be dug out by special therapy
Muscles and tissues store memories of events, which massage can release
questions.explanation_en: The title doesn't mean cells hold a recording; resting heart rate, breathing, muscle tone, and stress-hormone baselines get set to wartime and don't come back down. The article calls 'memories stored in muscles' the most abused misreading, and flags 'recovering repressed memories' as highly contested: trauma is usually remembered too well.

questions.question: 范德考克给出的一个定义被文章称为全书最好的一句：创伤的反面是什么？
options: 遗忘：让那段经历不再被时时想起、反复闯入
理解：把那件事的来龙去脉彻底想明白、讲清楚
主动性：重新相信自己的动作能够改变所处的境况
快乐：重新体验到愉悦、满足和对生活的兴致
questions.explanation: 无助是创伤的核心体验，所以任何能恢复「我做了一件事，世界因此变了一点」的活动都是治疗：划船、击鼓、排戏、在合唱里跟上拍子。「想明白」属于自上而下的路径，书里说它在警报响起时恰恰够不着。
questions.question_en: The article calls one of van der Kolk's definitions the best line in the book: what is the opposite of trauma?
options_en: Forgetting: no longer having the experience intrude again and again
Understanding: thinking the whole event through and explaining it clearly
Agency: believing again that your actions can change your situation
Happiness: feeling pleasure, satisfaction, and zest for life again
questions.explanation_en: Helplessness is the core of trauma, so anything that restores 'I did something and the world changed a little' is therapy: rowing, drumming, staging a play, keeping time in a choir. 'Figuring it out' is the top-down route, which the book says can't reach you when the alarm is ringing.
